chapter_theme: Sattaimuni Njanam, six verses attributed to Sattaimuni, teach a Siddhar's puja against the common kinds: not with a book, a lamp, a woman or a drawn chakra but with the Meru of forty-three triangles, through a ladder of goddess-mantras (Balai, Tripurai, Bhuvanai, Yamalai), five initiations, and then vaasi yoga that yields kaya siddhi. The last two verses turn to lament: the world dies and is born like a kavadi carried back and forth, and the poet asks his mind when maya will leave and tells it to look at the root.
structure_note: 1607 and 1608 contrast kinds of puja and warn that teaching the Meru openly loses the siddhis; 1609 and 1610 give the order of mantras, initiations and breath; 1611 and 1612 are complaints to the mind that end by pointing at the root (மூலம்).

1607.reading: Listen to the ways of puja: some do it by rote with a palm-leaf book in hand, some set a lamp, some win fame doing puja with a woman set before them, some worship a chakra; our puja is like the Meru, with the forty-three triangles set out, and that is how the Siddhars themselves worship.
1607.nuance: நாற்பத்துமுக்கோணம் (forty-three triangles) is the count of the Sri Chakra, whose raised form is called Meru, so the plain reading is a Sri Vidya diagram. The Siddhars also call the spine Meru, and the verse's 'our puja' may mean worship in the body rather than on a drawn plate; both readings stand. பெண்ணை வைத்தும், puja with a woman, names a left-hand rite without comment.

1608.reading: Those who worship the Meru that is the self: if they curse, the whole cosmos burns like fire; the Meru that is honey needs initiation, and a mere boy cannot touch it; but when one who worshipped the Meru that is the sky opened his mouth and taught it, his disciple plundered the alchemical siddhi and the siddhi of the sky, the one who spoke said.
1608.nuance: Three Merus are named, தான் (self), தேன் (honey) and வான் (sky), probably grades of the same worship, but the verse does not explain them. கவன சித்தி is unclear: ககன (sky-walking) or கவனம் (attention). The last two lines are a cautionary tale about open teaching: the disciple took the powers, so the Meru is to be kept in cipher.

1609.reading: Hear the three letters of Balai I spoke of; know the sign, do her puja, then hear more: hear the eight letters of Tripurai, who changed, and worship her, son; hear the letter of Bhuvanai, who is settled, and worship her with skill; hear the six letters of Yamalai, who is calmed, praise her feet and worship.
1609.nuance: The verse gives the syllable counts of four goddess-mantras and never the syllables: Balai three, Tripurai eight, Bhuvanai (Bhuvaneswari) one, Yamalai six. Tradition supplies them from the Sri Vidya and Yamala traditions, and the sequence is a graded initiation from the girl-goddess to the full form. The participles கூறிய, மாறிய, தேறிய, ஆறிய may be only rhyme-fillers.

1610.reading: After that hear the five letters of Yamalai; when the five initiations are finished in due form, set yourself to the yoga called vaasi, son, and pranayama is completed; knowing all this, there is no obstacle, none, to the siddhi of the body; what is the world the Siddhars spoke of, best of men: it takes up again what was left unfinished, see.
1610.nuance: The order is mantra and initiation first, breath second, and the body-siddhi (காயசித்தி, the deathless body) as the fruit. விட்டகுறை எடுக்கும், taking up what was left off, is usually said of practice resumed from a former birth; here it may mean the Siddhars' world completes what one left undone. Yamalai has six letters in 1609 and five here, which may be two mantras or a slip.

1611.reading: The fierce barbarians who roar and chase ... sink in pleasure; bewildered within the four states, when will the mind become straight, when will it know? Crores in the world hesitated; dying and being born became like a kavadi carried back and forth; drowned in sorrow, knowledge is gone; it is like knowing only in the burning ground: sheer void.
1611.nuance: The first line is corrupt (கெர்சித்துத் துரத்துச் சண்ணுஞ்) and the reading of it is a guess. நாலுபாதம் may be the four states of consciousness or the four feet (stages) of a path. The காவடி image, the pole carried back and forth on pilgrimage, makes rebirth a shuttling; சுத்தப் பாழ், the pure void, is here a verdict on wasted lives, not the yogic void.

1612.reading: When will the ruinous maya go and cease? When will the scattered mind come straight? When will I stand free of the infatuation that joins the woman with sword-like eyes? Mind, alas! When will all the desire for this hard world be cut at the root? Leaving the planet-like instruments you keep thinking on, look upward; and what it is that joins there, look at the root to see.
1612.nuance: Each எப்போ (when) is addressed to the mind, in the manner of the Pattinathar and Pambatti laments. கருவி (instruments) is the Siddhanta word for the tattvas, and கோளான, planet-like, makes them fates that circle one. The answer given is a direction: மேலே நோக்கி, மூலம் பாரே, look up and look at the root, the mooladhara, which the next work (ch 84) takes up at length.

links.note: Sattaimuni ends by telling the mind to look at the root; Thirumula Nayanar Njanam says how: look at the foot called the root within the subtle, through the adharas, to the place between the eyes and the brow.

Both make the body-siddhi (காயசித்தி) follow initiation: here after the five dikshas and vaasi yoga there is no obstacle to it; the Valluvar text says its first initiation was done and the siddhi burned off karma.

Two sides of the guru-disciple trade going wrong: here the teacher who speaks the Meru openly is plundered of his siddhis by the disciple; in Sivavakkiyar the madman who hands out gurus and the disciple who takes one are both beaten.

source_issues: 1611 line 1 is corrupt (தியங்கினால் கெர்சித்துத் துரத்துச் சண்ணுஞ்); the reading of the line is a guess.
1609 gives Yamalai six letters and 1610 five; either two mantras are meant or one count is a slip.
